verdicts.flaw_description: The outcome measure spans untreated units: "Hours cover every bearing position on each machine, and about a third of each machine's positions had spells on the old bearing." So the 340/290/410/260 extra hours are machine-level totals in which roughly a third of the positions were running the old bearing, and cannot be attributed to the redesign.

Two of the four cases measure the outcome before the line was fitted: block One was "fitted 3 August" but scored "by 18 June" of that summer, and block Three was "fitted 2 May" but scored "by 17 March" of that spring (cases Two, 8 Dec to 23 Feb, and Four, 7 Sep to 22 Nov, run forward, so the season windows are within-season). Half the evidence records a gain that predates the treatment.

A named alternative cause reaches every unit: "Pollen and airborne irritants in each group's district fell by half from the previous quarter, and every group lived and slept in unfiltered district air." Halved irritant exposure would by itself lower attack counts against the prior quarter, so the 4-7 fewer attacks are not attributable to the inhaler.

The retention numbers cover a population a third of which never received the treatment: "Retention figures cover every signup, email opened or not, and a third of each cohort's signups never opened it." A 3-6 point cohort-wide lift that includes non-openers cannot be credited to the onboarding email.

Two of the four classes are scored before the program started: Ashcombe "started the program 6 December" yet scored higher "by 11 September" of that autumn term, and Halloway "started the program 20 June" yet scored higher "by 24 April" of that spring term (Deerpark, 8 Jan to 12 Mar, and Marchfield, 6 Jul to 21 Aug, run forward within their named terms).
